questions.explain: Hyperscale decouples compute from storage: compute replicas hold only the buffer-pool cache, page servers shard the page space, a distributed log service handles commits, and Azure Premium Storage is the durable backing store.
options: Compute nodes own data files on local SSD
All replicas share one buffer pool
Compute replicas hold only the buffer pool; page servers shard page data; a distributed log service handles commits
The log service stores the data files directly
questions.q: Which statement correctly describes Hyperscale's decoupled storage architecture?

questions.explain: The chapter states the no-downgrade restriction is not merely technical — the Hyperscale storage format is fundamentally different from other tiers, and migration out requires export/import or backup/restore.
options: The service tier slider reverts instantly with no downtime
You cannot change back via a service tier change; migration out requires export/import or backup/restore
Downgrading takes 30 days to complete
Hyperscale can be downgraded to Business Critical but not General Purpose
questions.q: What does the chapter say about changing a Hyperscale database back to another service tier?

questions.explain: A named replica is an independent compute node with its own service tier, buffer pool, and connection string pointed at the same page servers — so no data copy is needed and creation takes minutes regardless of database size.
options: A full copy of the 50 TB database must be created first
It requires a new logical server in a different region
No data copy is needed — the new compute node reads from the existing page servers
The primary must be taken offline during replica creation
questions.q: Why does adding a named replica take minutes even for a 50 TB Hyperscale database?

questions.explain: Each Hyperscale vCore tier has a maximum log generation rate; exceeding it throttles transactions and produces LOG_RATE_GOVERNOR waits. Mitigate by scaling up vCores or reducing log generation (batching DML, minimally logged operations).
options: Scale up vCores to a tier with a higher log rate limit, or reduce log generation per unit of work
Enable trace flag 4606
Increase the auto-pause delay
Add more named replicas
questions.q: What should you do when a Hyperscale workload shows high LOG_RATE_GOVERNOR waits?

questions.explain: Backup storage redundancy (Local, Zone, Geo, GeoZone) can only be set at database creation — it cannot be changed afterward without creating a new database.
options: At any time via the Azure portal
Within the first 30 days
It changes automatically on failover
Only when the Hyperscale database is created
questions.q: When can Hyperscale's backup storage redundancy be set, per the chapter?
